**Handle an initial relay-feed failure before creating the webcam source.** When `webcamRelay.feed(webcamTrack)` resolves `false`, the encoder still uses `webcamRelay.track`. The direct camera track is selected only when relay construction returns `null`. This can leave the webcam output with no frames. Await the initial feed with the existing open timeout. Set the relay to `null` when it cannot deliver a first frame so the existing `webcamRelay?.track ?? webcamTrack` expression selects the direct track.
Suggested fix
```diff - const webcamRelay = webcamTrack && options.webcam ? createWebcamRelay() : null; - if (webcamRelay && webcamTrack) void webcamRelay.feed(webcamTrack); + let webcamRelay = webcamTrack && options.webcam ? createWebcamRelay() : null; + if (webcamRelay && webcamTrack) { + let timer: ReturnType | undefined; + const fed = await Promise.race([ + webcamRelay.feed(webcamTrack), + new Promise((resolve) => { + timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), WEBCAM_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS); + }), + ]); + clearTimeout(timer); + if (!fed) { + webcamRelay.stop(); + webcamRelay = null; + } + } ```
Committable suggestion
> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion // The encoder reads a relay track the camera feeds, so a camera turned off and on again // mid-take (a new camera track) still writes into the same file on the same clock. Without // a relay (no track processor or generator) it reads the camera track, as before. let webcamRelay = webcamTrack && options.webcam ? createWebcamRelay() : null; if (webcamRelay && webcamTrack) { let timer: ReturnType | undefined; const fed = await Promise.race([ webcamRelay.feed(webcamTrack), new Promise((resolve) => { timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), WEBCAM_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS); }), ]); clearTimeout(timer); if (!fed) { webcamRelay.stop(); webcamRelay = null; } } /** The camera track recording now: null while the camera is turned off mid-take. */ let webcamCamera: MediaStreamTrack | null = webcamTrack; releaseWebcam = () => { webcamCamera?.stop(); webcamRelay?.stop(); }; let webcam: { output: Output; source: MediaStreamVideoTrackSource; ```

**Guard the queued camera reopen against a newer off setting.** The off path runs immediately, but the reopen waits on `queue`. If the user turns the camera off before the queued callback starts, `turnWebcamOn()` re-enables `cameraWanted`, opens the camera, and feeds it into the recording. The `webcamOn` state remains false, so the existing engine request counter does not prevent this path. This can record webcam frames while the camera setting is off and can persist until the take ends.
Suggested fix
```diff --- "a/apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts" +++ "b/apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts" @@ -936,8 +936,10 @@ webcamOn = true; webcamParked = false; // On the queue, so an off that follows waits for this camera to open and releases it. queue = queue.then(async () => { + // Turned off again before this ran: the engine already holds the camera off. + if (!webcamOn) return; const result = await handle.turnWebcamOn(); if (result === "ok") { // Turned off again meanwhile: its gap goes on. if (webcamOn) gaps.close(takeTimeMs()); ```
Committable suggestion
> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion queue = queue.then(async () => { // Turned off again before this ran: the engine already holds the camera off. if (!webcamOn) return; const result = await handle.turnWebcamOn(); ```
